London, 10<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Platinum Australia** says that the treatment plant at its Smokey Hills platinum mine in South Africa, which produced its first concentrates in late January, is now expected to ramp up to its 60,000t/month design capacity.  In its interim report to end-December 2008, the company said that the treatment plant is expected to reach design capacity in the June quarter. PLA anticipates that the underground mine will achieve full production in early 2010.  At full capacity Smokey Hills is expected to produce 95,000oz/y 4E PGM, with estimated cash costs of US$300/oz, net of credits  and including smelting and refining charges.  As part of the company’s project financing agreement with Standard Bank Limited, PLA has hedged 26,960oz platinum and 29,1235oz palladium over the five year loan period at average prices of Rand15,411/oz and Rand4,339/oz respectively.  Work continues on the bankable feasibility study (BFS) of PLA’s Kalahari Platinum (Kalplats) project, but a number of development options are now being considered in the light of the currently depressed metal prices. This means that finalisation of the BFS will be delayed until the June quarter.  The company’s third PGM project is Panton in the Kimberley region of Western Australia. This has a JORC-compliant resource of 14.3m tonnes grading 5.2g/t 7E PGM; however, the project has been placed on hold pending a significant improvement in PGM prices. PLA reports a net loss of A$4.91m for the half-year compared with a loss of A$5.50m in the previous corresponding period. At December 31, the company had cash resources of A$11.54m but it has since raised a further A$14.58m through a placement of shares at 54 cents each in early February. _Source:  Platinum Australia_ 

**General Motors** factory workers in Canada will face a wage freeze through 2012, along with shorter vacations and higher contributions to benefit plans, under a tentative deal with GM Canada, the CAW said. Unionized workers will vote on the agreement this week. The Canadian units of GM and Chrysler LLC are seeking as much as C$10 billion ($7.78 billion) from the Canadian and Ontario governments to help them survive the crisis facing the auto sector. But the payments depend on the companies making savings that will include concessions from their unionized workers. GM Canada has already proposed a 10 percent cut in executive salaries, and reduced pay and benefits for salaried employees. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**China vehicle sales** surged 25%in February, the first gain in four months, after the government cut taxes on some models, helping the country extend its lead as the world’s largest auto market this year. Sales of passenger cars, buses and trucks climbed to 827,600, the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers said today. The tally in the first two months rose 2.7% to 1.56 million, compared with a 39% decline to 1.35 million in the U.S.  GM raise

d its forecast for China’s  market growth this year to between 5 and 10% from an earlier prediction of less than 3%.  Volkswagen AG said that it plans to double local sales by adding at least four new models a year until 2018. The carmaker sold 1.02 million vehicles in China last year. India also had an increase in February auto sales, the first gain in five months. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Ghabbour Auto** , the largest independent carmaker in the Middle East, said Q4 profit dropped 94 % due to slower sales of cars and buses in Egypt. 

**Global light-vehicle production** will likely slump 18 percent this year, hitting the lowest since 2001, as job losses and tighter credit deter car buyers, according to CSM Worldwide Inc. Output will drop to about 53 million vehicles this year from about 65 million last year, Michael Robinet, a vice president at the company, which advises automakers, said today. Sales may slightly surpass output as carmakers clear excess stock, he added. Production may post a “moderate” increase next year and then climb to 80 million units by 2015, as an economic recovery revives demand in the U.S. and Europe, Robinet said. Sales in the U.S. slid to the lowest rate since December 1981 last month. _Source:  Bloomberg_
